paragraphs: The Sprinter 314–319 CDI was offered during the VS30 pre-facelift era from 2018 to 2022, with two diesel engine options depending on the specification. Lower-output variants use the OM651 — a 2.1-litre four-cylinder diesel shared across the wider Mercedes commercial and passenger-car range of that era. Higher-output variants use the OM642 V6 diesel, a 3.0-litre unit with a well-established pattern for swirl flap and injector wear over time. Knowing which engine your van has matters because the components, the known wear patterns, and the rebuild specifics differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting. The 314–319 CDI was discontinued after 2022 when Mercedes replaced the V6 entirely with a 2.0-litre four-cylinder OM654 unit, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every SPRINTER 314–319 CDI on the road.

cards.body: A 2.1-litre four-cylinder diesel fitted to lower-output Sprinter 314–319 CDI variants from 2018 to 2022. Known for injector seal leaks and timing chain wear over time — see the callout above. We replace injector seals, timing chain components and gaskets as standard on every OM651 rebuild.

A 3.0-litre V6 diesel fitted to higher-output Sprinter 314–319 CDI variants from 2018 to 2022. Known for swirl flap and injector wear — see the callout above. We replace swirl flaps, injector seals and gaskets as standard on every OM642 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the Sprinter 314–319 CDI spans two distinct engines across this generation, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an OM651 part will work on an OM642 van — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic Sprinter quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
